about: Speed of ONE hardware thread (a vast.ai 'effective core') of each CPU model while every thread of the machine is busy, relative to one thread of an AMD EPYC 7502 (our measured reference machine) = 1.00.

compute: jobs whose tables fit in cache or a few hundred MB (exact solves from trick 2 on, equity sweeps, rollouts, tournaments). tt: jobs dominated by huge transposition tables (exact trick-1 solves, tens of GB per deal).

estimate = from published SPECrate2017_int results or mapped from a similar chip, before we measure. measured = written by our own benchmarks (python/tools/vast_market.py record); it always wins over the estimate.
uncertainty: rough relative error of the estimate (0.15 = +-15%).
Models are matched by the 'match' regular expression against vast.ai's cpu_name, first match wins.
spec_basis: SPECrate2017_int, speed of one copy with every hardware thread busy: compute = 531.deepsjeng_r (chess search with a hash table) and 541.leela_r (Go tree search); tt adds 505.mcf_r and 520.omnetpp_r (memory-latency heavy). Relative to EPYC 7502.
quota_note: Every vast.ai container we have run got a CPU quota of 96% of the offer's effective cores (61.4/64, 76.8/80, 122.9/128, 368.6/384); one host gave only half (see machines).

default.basis: unknown CPU: assumed slow until it is identified, so an unknown machine never tops a ranking by accident

observations.what: exact solver costs, same worlds as the 4-vCPU Xeon VM
observations.result: trick 3 median 8.8 ms, trick 2 median 2.8 s per world (Xeon VM: 8.8 ms, 3.1 s): same speed per thread when lightly loaded

observations.what: 4 trick-1 worlds, one at a time, all 368 threads on one world (solve_fast_par)
observations.result: 7 s, 32 s, 140 s, 25 s; about 0.5 million nodes/s per thread vs 3.6 million on 4 threads of the Xeon VM (world 0: 68 s on 4 threads): one world spread over 368 threads uses each thread at roughly 1/7 efficiency

observations.what: exact trick-1 PIMC, leader decisions, 4 worlds x 112 threads
exact trick-1 PIMC on different (possibly harder) decisions
observations.result: about 0.7 worlds per minute (in progress). SPEC predicts about the same speed per thread as the 9734, so the 2x gap per thread is mostly the decisions, not the machine
